U2: Python processor - integrate with Python for data computations.
U3: R processor - integrate with R.
U4: Hive sink - write data to Hive.
U5: Upgrade Spring Core to 4.1.1 (milestone) - dependency upgrade.
U6: Security definitions for REST API entity group/role access policies.
U7: ACLs for DSL Shell.
U8: ACLs for Admin UI.

These are varied. U5 is a dependency upgrade, likely straightforward but may require compatibility changes. U2 and U3 are similar investigation and integration. U6, U7, U8 are about security/ACL.

For ACLs, likely using Spring Security with method-level security or URL-based. For U1, we need to enable SSL and Basic auth on admin endpoints, probably using embedded server (Tomcat?) configuration. We'll structure:

Technical and design decisions:
- For Python integration: Use subprocess communication via stdin/stdout (pipe) to invoke Python scripts, as it's simpler and fits Spring XD model of modular processors. (Could also use Jython but limited to Python 2; subprocess is more flexible.)
- For R integration: Use rJava library to call R functions from Java, as it provides direct JNI integration and better performance for data transfer. Renjin is an alternative but may have compatibility issues. We'll assume rJava.
- For Hive sink: Use Hive JDBC driver to write data via INSERT statements or batch loading. Use Thrift if needed.
- For SSL/HTTPS and Basic auth: Configure embedded Tomcat (or Jetty) with SSL connector and Spring Security Basic auth filter on admin endpoints.
- For Spring Core upgrade: Update Maven/Gradle dependencies, resolve API changes, ensure compiled SpEL works (requires Spring 4.1+). Might need to update other dependent modules.
- For REST API security (U6): Use Spring Security with method-level @PreAuthorize annotations based on roles/groups. Define security definitions in configuration.
- For ACLs on DSL Shell and Admin UI (U7, U8): Implement a permission evaluation system using Spring Security ACLs or a custom permission checker. For shell, intercept commands; for UI, use URL-based security.

- The project already has Spring Security dependency.
- The team has access to Python and R runtimes for testing.
- Hive cluster is available for testing.

- Testing includes unit tests and integration tests with mocked dependencies.
- Documentation includes user guide updates and API docs.

- U5 upgrade may require minor code changes but no major refactoring.

U8: ACLs for Admin UI. Similar to U7 but for UI endpoints. Need to secure REST endpoints exposed to UI. Effort: Implementation 6h, testing 4h, doc 2h → 12h.

- Documentation (user guide, API docs) consolidation: 8h
- Code review and refactoring (self-review): 4h

technical_and_design_decisions: For Python processor (U2): Use subprocess communication via stdin/stdout to invoke Python scripts, as it fits the Spring XD model and avoids JVM limitations with CPython.
For R processor (U3): Use rJava library for direct JNI integration to call R functions, leveraging its performance and existing Java-R bridge.
For Hive sink (U4): Use Hive JDBC driver with connection pooling and batch inserts to write data efficiently.
For SSL/HTTPS and Basic auth (U1): Configure embedded Tomcat with SSL connector and Spring Security Basic authentication filter on admin endpoints.
For Spring Core upgrade (U5): Update Maven dependencies, resolve API changes, and enable compiled SpEL if supported by Spring 4.1.1 milestone.
For REST API security (U6): Use Spring Security method-level @PreAuthorize annotations with role/group-based access policies defined in configuration.
For ACLs on DSL Shell (U7): Implement a custom permission evaluator that intercepts shell commands and checks against Spring Security context.
For ACLs on Admin UI (U8): Secure UI REST endpoints using URL-based Spring Security filters and permission checks.

Hive cluster is accessible for integration testing of the Hive sink.
All estimates assume a single experienced developer working full-time.
Each user story includes investigation, design, implementation, unit/integration testing, and documentation.
The Spring Core upgrade (U5) requires only minor code adjustments and no major architectural changes.
No additional performance optimization or production hardening beyond functional correctness.
Documentation updates are limited to user guides and API documentation for the new features.

activities.activity_name: Implement U1 - SSL/HTTPS and Basic auth for admin endpoints
activities.activity_description: Enable SSL/HTTPS configuration and Basic authentication for administration endpoints to secure the application. Includes configuration properties, SSL setup, and Spring Security filter integration.

Investigate the best approach (subprocess via stdin/stdout) and implement a Python processor that allows data computations and statistical analysis. Includes spawning Python process, data passing, error handling, and configuration.
Investigate and implement an R processor using rJava library for direct Java-R integration. Includes calling R functions, data transfer, and configuration.
Implement a sink to write data into Hive using Hive JDBC driver with connection pooling and batch inserts. Includes driver setup, data mapping, and error handling.

activities.activity_name: Implement U5 - Spring Core upgrade to 4.1.1
activities.activity_description: Upgrade Spring Core dependency to version 4.1.1 milestone. Update Maven POM, resolve API changes, ensure compiled SpEL works, and verify compatibility with other modules.

activities.activity_name: Implement U6 - REST API security definitions
activities.activity_description: Define security definitions to configure entity (REST API) specific group/role access policies. Implement role-based access control using Spring Security method-level annotations and configuration.

activities.activity_name: Implement U7 - ACLs for DSL Shell
activities.activity_description: Implement ACL (Access Control List) capabilities to restrict access to resources (create/destroy/view streams) accessed via the DSL Shell. Integrate with Spring Security context.

activities.activity_name: Implement U8 - ACLs for Admin UI
activities.activity_description: Implement ACL capabilities to restrict access to resources accessed via the Admin UI. Secure REST endpoints exposed to the UI with Spring Security filters and permission checks.
Perform end-to-end integration testing across all user stories to ensure correct interaction between components, including cross-feature scenarios and error handling.
Compile and update user documentation, API references, and configuration guides for all new features implemented in this increment.
Perform self-review of all code changes, refactor where necessary, and ensure coding standards and best practices are followed.
